name: Dullness and dehydration
summary: Skin that looks tired often needs hydration and renewal rather than active treatment, and tends to respond well to a consistent, well-matched daily routine.
statement: Skin that looks tired often needs *hydration and renewal* rather than active treatment, and tends to respond well to a consistent, well-matched daily routine.
happening: Skin that looks dull or tired is often simply due to a slower cell renewal cycle or reduced hydration at the surface, rather than any deeper concern. This is usually one of the more responsive concerns to address, though the right approach depends on whether the underlying issue is hydration, renewal, or both.

factors.title: Cumulative exposure
factors.text: Dullness and dehydration usually reflect cumulative exposure and skin behaviour over years, not a single recent cause.

factors.title: Barrier and turnover
factors.text: Changes to the skin barrier and cell turnover rate influence how visible dullness and dehydration become over time.

factors.title: Individual variation
factors.text: How dullness and dehydration present and respond to treatment varies meaningfully between skin types.

recommendedText: Considered as a primary option for dullness and dehydration, combining cleansing and hydration in one treatment.
alongsideText: Often assessed alongside, since these concerns frequently share the same treatment options.

steps.title: Assessment first
steps.text: We look at hydration, renewal and routine together, since tired-looking skin rarely has a single cause.

steps.title: Hydration and renewal
steps.text: Treatment focuses on hydration and gentle renewal rather than more intensive work.

steps.title: A consistent routine
steps.text: A well-matched daily routine carries the result between treatments.

steps.title: Ongoing review
steps.text: The plan is reviewed at follow-up and adjusted as needed.
